l.i: Noster amor cultis, & amoenis coepit in hortis: Crescit florifero tempore consitus.
Permulcétque meos sensus, & odoribus auras: His, his, tam nitidis vatibus inferor.
Atque placent docto Beza mea carmina, spirant Iacmoti lepidos iam quia spiritus.
Iungamus Iacomote animos, iungamus, amemus: Quicquid Musa negat iunctus amor facit.

page.notes: The first line of the verse is a large woodcut initial "I" (decorated, partly illegible) joined to "Vngamus", read as "Iungamus" with the initial letter; the opening word of the poem is partly obscured by the initial. Several words in the verse (e.g. "Iacmoti", "Vatibus") are copied as printed. The signature "F ij" appears at right below the last line.
